_about: THE DEPTHS channel data. type: company | giant | event | wreck | acquired (needs 'by'). form: whale (giants), manta (companies), jelly (products and tech, default). region: where it started. year can be fractional to order events within a year. size scales creatures (1-4).

species.name: UNIVAC I
species.blurb: The first commercial computer built in the US. It called the 1952 election on live TV.

species.name: LEO I
species.blurb: A tea-shop chain, J. Lyons, builds its own computer to run payroll and stock. The first business computer.

species.name: IBM
species.blurb: Founded in 1911. For decades, computing simply meant IBM.

species.name: Fortran
species.blurb: The first widely used high-level language, built for scientists.

species.name: COBOL
species.blurb: Business logic in English-like code. It still runs banks today.

species.name: IBM System/360
species.blurb: One architecture across a family of machines. Software could finally outlive its hardware.

species.name: TCS
species.blurb: Tata starts a computer services unit in Mumbai. India's IT services industry begins here.

species.name: Unix
species.blurb: Built at Bell Labs on a spare minicomputer. Its ideas still run nearly everything.

species.name: ARPANET
species.blurb: Four computers connected. The first breath of the internet.

species.name: IBM unbundles software
species.blurb: IBM starts pricing software separately from hardware. The software industry is born.

species.name: PDP-11
species.blurb: DEC's minicomputer brings computing into labs and universities.

species.name: Xerox PARC
species.blurb: Invents the GUI, Ethernet, and the laser printer. Others get rich from them.

species.name: SAP
species.blurb: Five ex-IBM engineers in Germany build standard business software. Every big company's back office follows.

species.name: Microsoft
species.blurb: Gates and Allen sell a BASIC for the Altair.

species.name: Apple
species.blurb: Two Steves in a garage. The Apple II makes personal computers mainstream.

species.name: HCL
species.blurb: Six engineers in Delhi build Indian-made computers, years before the PC.

species.name: Oracle
species.blurb: Turns the relational database into a business.

species.name: Apple II and the 1977 trinity
species.blurb: Apple II, Commodore PET and TRS-80 all ship. Computers become things you buy in a shop.

species.name: VisiCalc
species.blurb: The first spreadsheet and the first killer app. People buy computers just to run it.

species.name: Wipro
species.blurb: A vegetable oil company from Bengaluru moves into computers, and later into software services.

species.name: IBM PC and MS-DOS
species.blurb: IBM makes the PC legitimate. Microsoft keeps the rights to DOS.

species.name: Infosys
species.blurb: Seven engineers start it in Pune with 10,000 rupees, borrowed from a founder's wife's savings.

species.name: Adobe
species.blurb: PostScript makes desktop publishing possible.

species.name: Minitel
species.blurb: France puts free online terminals in millions of homes, a decade before the web.

species.name: ZX Spectrum
species.blurb: A cheap British home computer. A generation of European game developers starts on it.

species.name: Macintosh
species.blurb: The graphical interface reaches ordinary people.

species.name: Windows 1.0
species.blurb: Microsoft puts windows on top of DOS.

species.name: Huawei
species.blurb: Starts in Shenzhen reselling phone switches, then builds its own.

species.name: ARM
species.blurb: A Cambridge spin-off designs low-power chips. Today nearly every phone runs on its designs.

species.name: World Wide Web
species.blurb: Tim Berners-Lee, at CERN near Geneva, publishes the first website.

species.name: Linux
species.blurb: A student's hobby kernel. It now runs most of the world's servers.

species.name: Nokia's GSM phone
species.blurb: Finland's Nokia ships the first mass-made GSM phone. Europe leads mobile for the next 15 years.

species.name: Commodore
species.blurb: Made the best-selling home computer ever, the C64. Bankrupt in 1994.

species.name: Netscape
species.blurb: The browser that starts the gold rush.

species.name: Amazon
species.blurb: Starts out selling books online.

species.name: Lotus
species.blurb: IBM buys Lotus, maker of the 1-2-3 spreadsheet.

species.name: Zoho
species.blurb: Started in Chennai as AdventNet. Grows into a global software suite without outside funding.

species.name: Yandex
species.blurb: A Russian search engine that beat Google in its home market.

species.name: Rakuten
species.blurb: An online mall from Tokyo, starting with 13 shops.

species.name: Google
species.blurb: PageRank brings order to the web.

species.name: DEC
species.blurb: Compaq buys Digital Equipment, the minicomputer pioneer.

species.name: Tencent
species.blurb: Starts in Shenzhen with QQ, an instant messenger. Later builds WeChat.

species.name: Netscape
species.blurb: AOL buys Netscape after the browser war is lost.

species.name: Y2K
species.blurb: The world races to fix two-digit years. Indian IT firms win huge contracts, and the outsourcing era takes off.

species.name: Alibaba
species.blurb: Jack Ma and 17 others start it in a Hangzhou apartment, to connect Chinese factories with buyers.

species.name: Salesforce
species.blurb: No software to install. Subscriptions start replacing boxed licenses.

species.name: Naver
species.blurb: A Korean search portal that Google never managed to beat.

species.name: Dot-com crash
species.blurb: The bubble bursts. Thousands of startups sink within months.

species.name: Baidu
species.blurb: China's search engine, founded in Beijing.

species.name: Pets.com
species.blurb: Shut down within a year of going public. The symbol of the crash.

species.name: Wikipedia
species.blurb: Anyone can edit. Open collaboration at world scale.

species.name: Agile Manifesto
species.blurb: Seventeen developers at a ski lodge rewrite how teams ship software.

species.name: Atlassian
species.blurb: Two Sydney graduates start it on a credit card. Jira follows.

species.name: Skype
species.blurb: Built by engineers in Tallinn. Free calls over the internet.

species.name: Firefox
species.blurb: Open source takes back the browser.

species.name: Facebook
species.blurb: Social networking goes mainstream.

species.name: Git
species.blurb: Linus Torvalds writes a version control system in about two weeks.

species.name: Android
species.blurb: Google quietly buys a small mobile OS startup.

species.name: YouTube
species.blurb: Google buys YouTube for $1.65 billion.

species.name: Shopify
species.blurb: Built in Ottawa to sell snowboards online. The store software became the business.

species.name: AWS
species.blurb: Rent servers by the hour. Startups no longer need data centers.

species.name: Spotify
species.blurb: A Stockholm answer to music piracy: make legal streaming easier than downloading.

species.name: iPhone
species.blurb: The phone becomes a computer in your pocket.

species.name: Flipkart
species.blurb: Two ex-Amazon engineers in Bengaluru start by selling books online.

species.name: Netscape Navigator
species.blurb: AOL ends support for the browser that started it all.

species.name: App Store
species.blurb: Software distribution changes overnight.

species.name: GitHub
species.blurb: Code hosting becomes social.

species.name: Android
species.blurb: The first Android phone ships. Open mobile, at huge scale.

species.name: Azure
species.blurb: Microsoft's cloud.

species.name: Sun Microsystems
species.blurb: Oracle buys Sun, and with it Java and MySQL.

species.name: Stripe
species.blurb: Online payments in a few lines of code.

species.name: Skype
species.blurb: Microsoft buys Skype for $8.5 billion.

species.name: Instagram
species.blurb: Facebook buys a 13-person photo app for $1 billion.

species.name: Minitel
species.blurb: France switches off Minitel after 30 years.

species.name: Docker
species.blurb: Ship the whole environment in a container.

species.name: Slack
species.blurb: Work chat that developers actually want.

species.name: WhatsApp
species.blurb: Facebook buys WhatsApp for $19 billion.

species.name: Nokia's phones
species.blurb: Microsoft buys the fallen phone giant.

species.name: Kubernetes
species.blurb: Google open-sources how it runs containers at scale.

species.name: OpenAI
species.blurb: Founded as a nonprofit AI research lab.

species.name: UPI
species.blurb: India launches instant phone payments. Within years it handles billions of payments a month.

species.name: BlackBerry phones
species.blurb: BlackBerry stops designing its own phones.

species.name: The Transformer
species.blurb: The paper "Attention Is All You Need" lays the foundation for modern AI.

species.name: GitHub
species.blurb: Microsoft buys GitHub for $7.5 billion.

species.name: Flipkart
species.blurb: Walmart buys most of Flipkart for $16 billion.

species.name: Windows Phone
species.blurb: Microsoft ends support for its last mobile OS.

species.name: Flash
species.blurb: Reaches end of life on the last day of 2020.

species.name: Anthropic
species.blurb: An AI safety company. Maker of Claude.

species.name: GitHub Copilot
species.blurb: AI starts writing code inside the editor.

species.name: ChatGPT
species.blurb: An estimated 100 million users in about two months.

species.name: Mistral
species.blurb: Paris AI lab releasing open-weight models.

species.name: MCP
species.blurb: An open standard for connecting AI agents to tools and data.

species.name: DeepSeek R1
species.blurb: A Chinese lab releases a strong reasoning model as open weights, cheap to run.
